text.p: Ameritech Corp on Tuesday said it notified federal regulators that it was withdrawing its application to provide long-distance telephone service in Michigan.
The decision came after the Federal Communications Commission on Friday said it would not consider key evidence submitted by Ameritech as part of the application.

Under the new U.S. telecommunications act, Ameritech and the other regional Baby Bells must prove to regulators that they have opened their local phone monopolies to competitors before they can gain access to the long-distance market.
The FCC on Friday noted that Michigan regulators had not yet approved Ameritech's "interconnection" agreement with AT&T Corp at the time of Ameritech's most recent filing.
In a statement Tuesday, Ameritech said it expected the status of its contract with AT&T in Michigan to be resolved.
